overview.purpose: slop bundles multiple source files into a single markdown file for transmission to AI systems. Your role is to deserialize (deslop) these files, perform requested tasks, and reserialize (reslop) the results.
workflow: Receive a slopified (.slop or .md) file containing multiple source files
Parse the block headers to reconstruct the original files
Perform the requested tasks (analysis, modifications, debugging, etc.)
Reslop only modified/new files back into a slop file

Return the slop file: in a chat context emit it as a single fenced code block (language tag `slop` or none) so markdown will not misrender #SLOP/#SLOP_META lines as headers; with tool/disk access write it to a .md file.

slop_format_specification.description: A slop file contains zero or more meta blocks (first) followed by zero or more file blocks. Blocks concatenate directly — no blank lines between them.

components.path: Original absolute path, JSON-encoded (backslashes→\\, quotes→\"). Preserve exactly on reslop.
components.SLOP_PARTIAL_LINES: Optional. Replaces only lines s–e (1-indexed, inclusive) of the existing file. Omit for full-file blocks.
components.SLOPED_LINES: Exact count of content lines immediately following this header.
components.SLOP_TRAILING_NEWLINE: 1 = file ends with \n, 0 = it does not. Always serialize as 0 or 1.
components.SLOP_BASE_SHA: Optional. blake3 hash of the file at slop time (64-char hex). When returning a PARTIAL block, carry this forward unchanged so the host can detect on-disk drift. Omit on redacted or read-only files.
components.SLOP_READONLY: Optional. true = context-only block. Read and honor it, but NEVER modify it and NEVER emit it in reslopified output.

meta_block_header.description: Carries machine-readable metadata (e.g. a codegraph). Generated by slop -g (equivalent long form: --include-graph). Always appears before file blocks. Parse N lines of content then SKIP — do not write to disk. Do not emit meta blocks yourself.

deslop.description: Convert a slop file back into the original files.
algorithm: 2. Meta block: extract SLOP_META_LINES N, consume exactly N content lines, discard — do not write.
3. File block: extract path (JSON-decode), optional partial range, SLOPED_LINES N, trailing-newline flag.
4. Consume exactly N content lines after the header.
5. Full block (no partial range): join lines with \n, append \n if flag=1. Create parent dirs. Write to disk.

6. Partial block: read target file as it currently exists on disk (reflecting any prior partial edits to it). Replace lines s–e (1-indexed) with the block's content lines. Write merged result back. If you have no tool/disk access you must already know the full content of the target file (from an earlier full block in this slop, a prior slop in the session, or your own prior writes); if none of those hold, do not guess — ask the user to resend a full block for that file.
7. Repeat until all blocks are processed.
implementation_notes: Partial blocks require the target file to exist and be long enough to cover end_line.
Multiple partial blocks on the same file are applied in document order; each sees the result of the previous.

reslop.description: Convert modified files back into a slop file. Only emit files you modified or created.
algorithm: 1. Identify all files modified or created during your work.
2. For each file, choose full or partial output:
FULL — rewritten or new file: read content, count lines, emit header then all content lines.
PARTIAL — localized change in a large file: emit header with SLOP_PARTIAL_LINES, then replacement lines only.
3. Concatenate all blocks directly (no blank lines between) into a .md output.

line_counting.rule: Strip trailing \n if present, split remainder on \n, count segments. Empty string = 0 lines.

partial_block_notes: Trailing-newline flag reflects the WHOLE file's state after the edit, not just the replacement lines.
When emitting multiple partial blocks for the same file, line numbers in later blocks must account for line-count changes caused by earlier partial blocks.
Emit multiple partial blocks for the same file in ascending start_line order.
Choose FULL vs PARTIAL by replacement size: if replacement lines >= 50% of the file, emit a FULL block; otherwise prefer PARTIAL (even for interleaved edits).

Safety valve: if multiple partials on the same file would require complex line-shift bookkeeping (e.g. interleaved edits with large deltas), prefer a single FULL block over risky shifted partials — correctness outranks brevity.
implementation_notes: Serialize trailing newline as 0 or 1 (never true/false).
JSON-escape file paths (use JSON string serialization).
Do not re-emit unchanged files unless the user asks.
Do not emit #SLOP_READONLY true blocks — those are context-only; never reslop them.
Carry #SLOP_BASE_SHA forward unchanged when returning partial blocks for the same file.
reslop.delivery: In a chat context, emit the reslopified output as a single fenced code block with language tag `slop` (or no language) so #SLOP/#SLOP_META lines are not rendered as headers. Do not split across multiple code blocks. With tool/disk access, write to a .md file at the user's chosen path.

requesting_files.rule: The repo-map meta block may reference files NOT present as editable #SLOP blocks. Those are context only. If you need the full contents of such a file to complete the task, do NOT infer or hallucinate them — request the file by emitting a line in your text response (not inside a slop block):
requesting_files.note: The user can then re-slop with that file included (e.g. slop --seed <path> ...). This is a convention, not a parser change to slop files.

host_integration.auto_deslop: #SLOP_AUTO_DEslop is NOT a tag that appears inside a slop file. Auto-deslop is a host-side config flag (slop auto_deslop: true in the host's config) that registers a filesystem rule: any *.slop.md file landing in the watched downloads folder is automatically deslopified via `slop -d __FILE__`. If you ever encounter the literal string #SLOP_AUTO_DEslop inside a slop body, treat it as ordinary file content — it is not part of this spec and carries no meaning for your parser.

practical_examples.with_meta_block:
#SLOP_META "repo-graph" #SLOP_META_KIND codegraph #SLOP_META_FORMAT repomap #SLOP_META_LINES 1 #SLOP_META_READONLY true
<graph data — skip, do not write>
#SLOP "/tmp/index.js" #SLOPED_LINES 1 #SLOP_TRAILING_NEWLINE 0
console.log('hi');

error_handling.malformed_header: Report the line number and problematic content to the user.
error_handling.line_count_mismatch: Report expected vs. actual line count and the affected file path.
error_handling.invalid_partial_range: Report if start > end, either value is 0, or end exceeds existing file length.
error_handling.missing_metadata: Report which of SLOPED_LINES or SLOP_TRAILING_NEWLINE is absent and the affected path.

best_practices: Validate slop block headers before consuming file content.
Track modifications carefully so you can reslop accurately.
Create parent directories automatically when desloping.
Line counts must be exact — off-by-one errors corrupt the slop file.
Handle the trailing newline flag correctly; it is essential for exact file restoration.
Empty files: #SLOPED_LINES 0 #SLOP_TRAILING_NEWLINE 0 with no content lines.
Prefer partial blocks for large files with small changes to reduce output size.
Add any newly created files to the reslopified output even if they weren't in the original slop.
If the user requests specific files, only reslop those files.
